findings.title: Engineering carries disproportionate Security-review drift
findings.evidence: Engineering represents 19.3% of purchase volume but 48.1% of Security-review violations (180 of 374).
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Technology purchases use team-specific intake paths that do not consistently invoke the central Security gate.
findings.recommendation: Move Security eligibility evaluation to submission time and block PO creation when a required review is absent.
findings.kpi: Security-review compliance by department and category

findings.title: The July update improved Vendor Validation
findings.evidence: Applicable Vendor Validation violations fell from 17.4% before the update to 5.7% after it, a decrease of 11.7 points.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: NovaProcure's enforced vendor gate reduced a control gap that had been optional in the legacy workflow.
findings.recommendation: Retain the vendor gate and accelerate retirement of remaining legacy routing.
findings.kpi: Vendor Validation violation rate by source system

findings.title: Urgent routing introduced a Procurement side effect
findings.evidence: Procurement-related violation incidence among urgent requests changed from 3.7% before the update to 10.4% after it.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The new fast-track branch prioritizes cycle time but does not always rejoin the mandatory Procurement gate.
findings.recommendation: Add a non-bypassable Procurement eligibility check to urgent routing and regression-test the branch.

findings.title: Austin shows a legacy travel-threshold adoption gap
findings.evidence: After July, travel requests between $5,000 and $7,500 had a 57.1% Finance-rule violation rate in Austin versus 12.5% elsewhere.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: A material share of Austin traffic remains on ProcureFlow Classic, which still applies the former $7,500 threshold.
findings.recommendation: Migrate Austin routing and add an effective-date configuration check to deployment validation.
findings.kpi: Post-change compliance by office and source system

findings.title: Marketing uses exceptions at an elevated rate
findings.evidence: Marketing's exception rate is 2.7% compared with 1.2% company-wide.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Late campaign intake and vendor timing pressure make competitive-bid exceptions a normalized workaround.
findings.recommendation: Introduce earlier campaign procurement intake and require structured exception reason codes.
findings.kpi: Exception and undocumented-exception rates by department

findings.title: Segregation-of-duties signals concentrate in Revenue
findings.evidence: Revenue accounts for 67.9% of self-approval indicators (129 of 190).
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Delegated approver configuration in high-velocity commercial teams permits requester/approver identity overlap.
findings.recommendation: Enforce requester-versus-approver validation and audit delegated approval groups.

findings.title: Near-threshold clusters warrant human review
findings.evidence: The indicator logic identified 12 employee/vendor clusters totaling $340,538 across flagged transactions.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Clusters may reflect phased delivery, recurring purchases, budget timing, or threshold avoidance; the data alone cannot establish intent.
findings.recommendation: Route indicators to a documented, context-aware review process; do not automate adverse conclusions.
